evidence: AAJ 1979 (Tindall): broken north-face glacier, then a ridge to the right for 500 ft, 'an interesting snow traverse and a steep rock scramble to the summit'; Jack's easiest route is itself 'class 4, with exposure'.
note: No published grade for this line. Since the easiest route to Jack's summit is Class 4 and this one finishes on 'a steep rock scramble', Class 3 understates it; Class 4 is the floor. Searched MP, SummitPost, Mountaineers, AAJ 1979 text, Wikipedia; no TR of a repeat found.

evidence: SummitPost lists the North Ridge as Class 4: Class 3 from the Klawatti-Austera col to The Smokestack, bypassed on the west; a TR says 'very exposed knife edge sections' needed 'good routefinding to keep the route at third class'.
note: Class 3 is possible with careful route-finding; the published rating is Class 4.

evidence: SummitPost: South Face Class 3-4, 45-50 deg snow through a constriction, slabs and a moat late season. TR: 'a short Class 4-5 rock pitch to clear the bergschrund and then... 40- to 55-degree snow', one rappel over the schrund. Another TR: 'very steep south-facing snow slope', icy, tricky bergschrund bridges.
note: Class 4 is the published top. In some years the bergschrund forces a short roped rock step that one party called Class 4-5, so the record's 5.2 breakdown pitch is a conditional low-5th step, not a published grade. The snow is 45-55 deg (steep snow, Class 3 by the brief).

evidence: Goatshead Spire (upper tower, east spur of Lemah Two; Goodman/Mason, Aug 8 1982) is documented only by location and FA; Lemah's summits all have Class 4-low 5th routes.
note: Searched 'Goatshead Spire', Goodman/Mason 1982, Lemah east spur towers, MP, SummitPost and the AAJ 1983 index (no Lemah entry). No grade or description exists online; 5.0 is the low-5th default for a rock tower on this massif.

evidence: Only a 1978 trip log names the 'West Face-West Rib' of The Lichtenhorn, with no rating. Recent TRs: the west pinnacle goes as 'a loose scrambly class 3 route that goes all the way around the spire'; the direct ridge had 'slick class 4/5'.
note: No source rates the west rib itself; Class 4 is the record's own 'short class 4 steps' on the rib. The summit is normally finished by the Class 3 wrap-around, not the low-5th direct.

evidence: A 2018 TR grades the Rankin Creek line AI3+: 30-40 deg snow, a 50-ft serac crux of '70-85 degree snow' over a crack bridge, a 60-deg hidden gully, snow arêtes, a 50-deg final gully. Other TRs: 60+ deg, a narrow gully 'the steepest slope of the route', tools and pickets, no grade.
note: The only numeric grade online is AI3+, from the TR whose pitch sequence the record's breakdown follows; others confirm the steep snow/ice character but give no grade.
identity: That AI3+ TR titles its climb 'East Face', but it describes the same Rankin Creek approach and the serac, hidden gully and arête sequence of the X Couloir / SW Face route, so it is a naming difference, not a different route.

evidence: Kellogg/Holsten: 'The south side of Little Mac looked like low fifth class, so we soloed up a few pitches... We simulclimbed up to 5.7 and soon reached the first summit.' SummitPost: the SW Arête is a 9-pitch route with only a two-line Beckey description.
note: The only numbered grade for Little Mac's south side is 5.7, from a Pickets enchainment account. It is not certain that party was on the exact SW Arête line, so confidence stays low. The record's 5.4 has no source. Searched MP, SummitPost, Peakbagger, Abegg's Pickets pages (blocked), Beckey 1969 FA.

evidence: AAJ: the South Couloir of Little Sister was skied as 'the proudest line' of a Twin Sisters high route, no angle given; the traverse's 4th-class rock and 50-deg ice crux was near South Twin. A 2015 winter ascent went via the east col and wrapped onto the south side; 'somewhat steep' snow to the col, no rating.
note: Mapped from the record's breakdown and the TRs: steep snow plus a little 3rd-class snow/rock near the summit, so Class 3. No published rating for this couloir. Searched MP, SummitPost, AAJ, Abegg (blocked), turns-all-year.

evidence: MP West Face (Berdinka, 6/21/2013): Easy 5th, Grade II, 1000 ft, 7 pitches, 'consistent 4th and low 5-th climbing... possibly tougher cruxes depending on route choice'.
note: Low 5th with no number anywhere, so 5.0 per the rule.

evidence: 2024 Ptarmigan TR: Lizard 'via the south ridge and descended via the west ridge. The climb is pretty straightforward, but somewhat loose class 2.' SummitPost: an easy ascent from the 6,800-ft pass on the south ridge.
note: The record's Class 3 'direct' variant has no source; the south ridge route as climbed is Class 2.

evidence: From the upper Richardson Glacier onto the East Ridge: 'a short class 4ish step' that is bypassed on ledges into 'a gully running parallel to the ridge crest (class 3)'; another TR: 'a rotten, 3rd class gully to the remote summit'; a 2025 TR: 'a couple of class 3 steps' near the summit.
note: The Class 4 step on the ridge is normally avoided, so the normal line is Class 3.

evidence: MP: Easy 5th, one 30 m pitch with three large bolts, 'many different variations, all which are easy'. TR: 'one full pitch (or two short pitches) of Class 4 or 5.0 climbing up the peak's southeastern ridge crest'.
MP: Easy 5th, Grade II; 'slabby depression (crux section, Class 4/5)'. TRs: 'Class 4... never too difficult'; low 5th only on off-route blocks; one party felt a north-side dihedral was about 5.4.
note: Low 5th with no number, so 5.0. Sources range from Class 4 to 5.0 on the normal line; 5.4 only off-route.

evidence: MP South Face (Crooks/Kennedy 1941): Easy 5th, Grade II, 4 pitches, 500 ft; 'several low-5th pitches lead to a slab; the final pitch after this is steeper.' The 5.10 'South Face Left' is a separate line.
note: Low 5th with no number, so 5.0. The record's 5.4/5.4/5.5/5.6 pitch breakdown is not supported by any source found.
